# Question

The collaborator studies how GLI-mediated Hedgehog signaling affects neuronal
progenitor differentiation. GLI is overexpressed, then perturbed or removed,
and gene expression is measured over a time course. Genes that respond were
grouped into **10 clusters** by their expression pattern (maSigPro).

**Hypothesis:** genes that respond to GLI perturbation are enriched for genes
implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders.

| Analysis | Approach | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Autism | Enrichment with SFARI gene sets (category 1, 2, 1&2) | done |
| Autism | High- vs medium-confidence TADA genes (Fu et al. 2022) | done |
| Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD) | Enrichment with Wang et al. 2022 NDD genes | done |
| Developmental disorders (DD only) | DD285 list | prepared, not run yet |
| Schizophrenia | MAGMA with GWAS summary statistics | planned |

# GLI-response clusters

All gene names were updated to current HGNC symbols. Only protein-coding genes
are kept, to match the background (below). Most dropped genes are lncRNAs,
antisense transcripts or pseudogenes.

```{r clusters}
tab <- data.frame(
  cluster = sort(unique(cl$cluster)),
  genes_in_file = as.vector(table(cl$cluster)),
  protein_coding_kept = as.vector(table(factor(cl$cluster[cl$kept], sort(unique(cl$cluster))))))
tab <- rbind(tab, data.frame(cluster = "total", genes_in_file = sum(tab$genes_in_file),
                             protein_coding_kept = sum(tab$protein_coding_kept)))
knitr::kable(tab, col.names = c("Cluster", "Genes in file", "Protein-coding genes kept"),
             format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

# Gene sets

Seven gene sets, chosen 11/17/2026. Details and sources are on the
[gene sets page](gene_sets.html).

```{r genesets}
def <- c(
  "TADA-high_fu2022"     = "Fu et al. 2022 TADA, autism FDR &le; 0.001",
  "TADA-med_fu2022"      = "Fu et al. 2022 TADA, 0.001 < autism FDR &le; 0.05",
  "TADA-high&med_fu2022" = "union of the two (= Fu's 185 autism genes)",
  "NDD_wang2022"         = "Wang et al. 2022, 615 NDD genes from de novo variants in 46,612 trios",
  "SFARI_cat1"           = "SFARI Gene, score 1 (release 07-12-2026)",
  "SFARI_cat2"           = "SFARI Gene, score 2",
  "SFARI_cat1&2"         = "union of the two")
n <- table(factor(gs$gene_set, names(def)))
knitr::kable(data.frame(names(def), unname(def), as.vector(n)),
             col.names = c("Gene set", "Definition", "Protein-coding genes"),
             escape = FALSE)
```

# Test

The test is **Fisher's exact test, two-sided**, as in the earlier rare-variant
analysis. For each cluster and gene set, the 2&times;2 table compares the cluster
with the *rest* of the background:

|                  | in gene set | not in gene set |
|------------------|:-----------:|:---------------:|
| in cluster k     | a | b |
| rest of background | c | d |

We use two backgrounds, because they answer different questions:

* **All protein-coding genes** (`r fmt(nrow(bg))` HGNC genes). Is cluster k
  enriched relative to the genome?
* **All clustered genes** (`r fmt(sum(cl$kept))`). Is cluster k enriched
  relative to the *other* GLI-responsive clusters? This is the stricter test. It
  partly controls for the fact that genes expressed in neural progenitors are
  generally enriched for neurodevelopmental genes.

FDR is Benjamini–Hochberg within each background (10 clusters &times; 7 gene
sets). The seven pooled "all clusters vs genome" tests are their own family. A
two-sided test flags depletion as well as enrichment, so results always show the
direction.

# Caveats and next steps

* **Background.** The ideal background is every gene measured in the
  experiment, not every protein-coding gene. If the collaborator can share
  that list, we will rerun with it.
* **The gene sets overlap.** SFARI, TADA and NDD share many genes, so
  results across gene sets are not independent.
* **Mutation-intolerant genes.** Many NDD genes are highly intolerant of
  damaging mutations. A cluster rich in such genes could look enriched for that
  reason alone. Next step: a test that accounts for this, using the
  constraint and haploinsufficiency lists.
* **Interpretation** needs the expression pattern of each cluster, e.g. up or
  down after GLI removal, from the collaborator.
